records.name: Japanese Christian Church of Philadelphia
records.summary: A congregation whose website is in Japanese and English, with Sunday worship in the building and on Zoom, and coffee and sometimes lunch afterward.
records.what_you_do: Attend Sunday worship in person or on Zoom, stay for coffee or lunch, or join the online Bible study that meets on the second and fourth Mondays.

schedule.text: Sunday worship at 11 am in the church building, with a Zoom service alongside

access.notes: The directions page names Overbrook station on the SEPTA R5 line, one stop past 30th Street Station, as the nearest stop, then gives walking directions to the church.

first_step.how: Come to the 11 am Sunday service at 6301 Drexel Road, in person or on Zoom, or call 215-473-1910 with questions before a first visit.
first_step.basis: The site says visitors of any faith and families with children are welcome, and it lists several ways to get in touch.
first_step.what_to_expect: Sunday worship starts at 11 am in the church building, and a Zoom service runs alongside it. The church mainly serves Japanese speakers, and the website is in Japanese and English. Coffee follows worship, and some Sundays also have a meal or lunch.
first_visit_tips: Parking is available, and the entrance is from Drexel Road.
Plan to stay for coffee, and for lunch on Sundays when a meal is listed.
From the 69th Street Terminal, take Bus 65 to 63rd Street and Sherwood Avenue, as the directions page explains.
Call 215-473-1910 before you come if you have questions.

records.notes: The October 2026 items (guest preachers, communion) sit under a September 2026 heading, so last_sign_of_life uses 2026-09. The email link on the contact page is obscured, so no email is recorded. No Zoom link or meeting ID is published on the pages read. The Bible study is online; the site says a further session may be added if attendance grows.

records.name: Jewish Children's Folkshul
records.summary: A secular Jewish community in Northwest Philadelphia for families and adults. Its Sunday school teaches Jewish history, holidays and values to children from kindergarten through high school, and adults can join study groups, outings and social clubs.
records.what_you_do: Enroll children in Sunday school, come to holiday celebrations and life-cycle events as a family, or join adult study groups, outings and social activities.

schedule.text: Sunday school meets most Sundays from 10 am to 12:30 pm, September through May.

locations.label: Northwest Philadelphia (street address shared by email)

cost.text: Yearly membership and Sunday school tuition, paid in full or in installments. Tuition assistance can be requested. The amounts are in a linked PDF.

first_step.how: Email Folkshul@folkshul.org for the meeting address and to ask about a visit. The calendar also lists an adult introduction session that is open to new people.
first_step.basis: The site says it wants new families and adults, and the calendar lists an adult introduction session that is open to new people, with an email address for questions.
first_step.what_to_expect: Sunday school runs about 10 am to 12:30 pm on most Sundays from September through May, with classes by grade and a free Sunday Fundays program for children ages 0 to 4 and their caregivers on select Sundays. Adults can join study groups, a restaurant club, local outings, film screenings and a speakers series, and the adult community gathers during Sunday school hours. Families register for membership first, then enroll each child and pay tuition, with tuition help available on request.
first_visit_tips: Email for the meeting address before you come, since it is not published on the website.
Membership comes before Sunday school enrollment, so ask about the steps early.
Most calendar items are for members, so ask whether a specific event is open to visitors.

records.notes: The calendar lists events from October 11 to November 8, 2026, which is the dated evidence used. Accessibility is not mentioned on any page read. The partners page (folkshul.org/partners) was not reviewed this pass. An Instagram account is listed on the join page; its link was not recorded.

records.name: Jewish Community of Rhawnhurst (JCOR)
records.summary: An Orthodox community network in Rhawnhurst, Northeast Philadelphia. It links six congregations, a kollel, chesed groups, schools, and mikvahs, and it shares the weekly eruv status.
records.what_you_do: Join the JCOR email group for announcements, shiurim, events, and job and housing listings. Check the weekly eruv status, or browse the shul directory to choose a congregation.

schedule.text: No set meeting times are listed. Shiurim and events are announced through the email group.

cost.text: No fee is listed for the email group. An optional $50 eruv sponsorship can be given through an online form.

first_step.how: Join the JCOR email group from the website, then choose one of the six congregations in the shul directory to visit.
first_step.basis: The site invites visitors and people thinking about moving to the area, and it gives a clear way to sign up for the email group.
first_step.what_to_expect: JCOR is a network rather than one group, so a first step is choosing a congregation from the directory on the page. Shiurim (Torah classes) are offered across the congregations and by the kollel, and the email group announces them along with events and job and housing postings. The site lists no visit times, so check with the congregation you pick before you go.
first_visit_tips: Check the weekly eruv status before Shabbat, since the site shares it through the email group.
Read the About section for information on schools, kosher options and housing if you are thinking of moving.
Contact the congregation you choose to ask about visiting.

records.notes: The Atom feed at jcor.org/feed.xml has no entries, so no calendar feed is recorded. The JCOR email group page on groups.io returned HTTP 402 and was not read, so the group's own message history is unverified. The site has no dated items, so status stays probably_active. Northeast Community Kollel has its own website and was not fetched this pass, so it is not listed as a lead; a later lead run should check it. The six shuls in the directory are listed in leads_only with the directory page as the link, since the directory gives no websites.

records.name: Jewish Graduate Student Network
records.summary: A Jewish community network for graduate students and young professionals in Philadelphia, run as a program of Philly Hillel. It lists programs named Shabbat Across Philly and Philly Jewish Community, along with student associations.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for the weekly e-newsletter, attend a home Shabbat dinner or holiday meal, or come to a lunch and learn or networking event. The site does not say how membership works.

schedule.text: Programs run through the academic year and over the summer: home Shabbat dinners, holiday dinners, lunch and learns and networking events. No fixed weekly time is listed.

locations.label: Home Shabbat dinners and events across the city

cost.text: No program fees are listed. The group asks for donations and corporate sponsorships.

first_step.how: Sign up for the weekly e-newsletter from the site, then email info@phillyhillel.org to ask how a newcomer can join a home Shabbat dinner or an event.
first_step.basis: Anyone can sign up for the weekly newsletter and email to ask questions, and the FAQ says young professionals can take part as well as grad students, but the site does not say newcomers get a special welcome.
first_step.what_to_expect: Most events are meals or discussions: home Shabbat dinners hosted by a grad student or young professional, holiday dinners, lunch and learns, and networking nights. The group says most participants are grad students, usually aged 22 to 35, and young professionals are welcome too. The site does not list costs or how long events last, and its calendar showed no upcoming events when we checked.
first_visit_tips: Sign up for the weekly e-newsletter so you hear about upcoming events.
Email info@phillyhillel.org before you come, since the site does not explain how guests join home dinners.
If the calendar is empty, call 267.229.1451 to ask about the next program.

records.notes: The site has no dated item. The only year is a 2022 copyright footer, which is not used as evidence, and the calendar lists no upcoming events. Status stays probably_active because the site works and gives no dates, so treat it with care and confirm with the group. Shabbat Across Philly pays hosts per guest; that is host information and is not recorded. The student associations (law, medical, dental, veterinary, nursing, business) are tied to individual school student governments, list no meeting times or contacts, and do not say whether non-students can join, so they are not added as leads.

records.name: Joseph R. Lynch Observatory public nights (Drexel University)
records.summary: Drexel's physics department opens its rooftop observatory to the public on the first Wednesday of most months during the school year, weather permitting. Everyone is invited, but the telescope is being replaced, so no public night is set right now.
records.what_you_do: Go up to the observatory roof at a listed night and look through the telescope when the sky is clear. Check the status page first, since no night is listed while the upgrade is under way.

schedule.text: First Wednesday of most months during the school year, about 30 minutes after sunset, weather permitting. Usually no public nights from July to September, and each night runs about two hours.

locations.label: Roof of the Main Building, Drexel University, entered at 32nd and Chestnut Streets

cost.text: No fee is listed on the pages checked.

access.notes: The route to the roof is up several flights of stairs, and no elevator is mentioned. The physics department at physics@drexel.edu handles accommodation questions.

first_step.how: Check the status page at drexel-observatory.vercel.app for a listed night, since none is set while the telescope is replaced. When one is listed, enter the Main Building at 32nd and Chestnut Streets and follow the stair directions on Drexel's physics page.
first_step.basis: Anyone can come, but no night is scheduled while the telescope is replaced, so the way in is unclear until dates return.
first_step.what_to_expect: A public night is a session on the Main Building roof, run by a physics professor with graduate and undergraduate helpers. Guests look through the observatory telescope at objects such as planets, star clusters, nebulae and comets, when the sky is clear. The route up is several flights of stairs, so plan for the climb.
first_visit_tips: Check the status page the day of: the night is cancelled or moved if it rains or the sky is not clear.
Expect several flights of stairs, since the site mentions no elevator.
Email physics@drexel.edu before you come if you have an access need.

records.notes: Public nights are paused. The status page says the dome has no telescope while an upgrade is completed, no dates are set until further notice, and a November 4 night depends on the new telescope being in place. That status page gives no year for the date, so it is not used as dated evidence. The nights page gives the monthly time slots, which the schedule text summarises. Neither page gives cost, age, RSVP or walk-in rules, so none are recorded. The GE Foundation link on the physics page is a funder, not a lead.

records.name: JSJ Food Bank
records.summary: A nonprofit that offers free meals and behavioral health programs for students in grades K to 12 and adults 55 and older in Philadelphia.
records.what_you_do: Students and older adults can ask about free meals and behavioral health programs. The group also lists free after school programs.

cost.text: The group describes its meals and programs as no cost.

first_step.how: Call 215-375-4558 to ask about free meals for students or adults 55 and older, or email info@jsjfoodbank.org about the youth after school programs.
first_step.basis: The site lists free meals and youth programs and gives a phone and email, but no sign-up steps, hours or meal times, so the way in is unclear.
first_visit_tips: Call before you go, since the site lists no office hours.
Ask whether any meal site is running now; the group ran free summer meals for kids under 18 in 2025.
The site also names a peer-led STEM program for youth, so ask about it if that interests your child.

records.notes: A CBS Philadelphia article dated June 18, 2025 names JSJ Food Bank as a summer meal provider for children under 18, serving more than 500 students a day in summer with a focus on Frankford. That is the newest dated evidence, so last_sign_of_life is 2025-06 and the summer program is not described as current. A directory listing for JSJ's Northwood Park site (1002 Arrott Street, Monday to Friday, from the 2025 USDA summer list) says walk-in and appointment requirements are not confirmed, so walk-ins are not recorded. The group's own site has no hours, sign-up steps or program pages. The one WebSearch was used for this gap. Staff names beyond the contact name and the Instagram handle are left out.

records.name: Junior Achievement of Southeastern Pennsylvania
records.summary: A nonprofit that brings lessons on money, work, and starting a business into schools and after-school programs. Volunteers from many kinds of jobs teach short classes and guide hands-on activities such as a budgeting simulation.
records.what_you_do: Sign up through the volunteer form, choose a grade range and a schedule with a program manager, and attend a short training. Then share your work and life experience in classes, in person or virtually.

schedule.text: Classes run during the school year. Times are set between each volunteer and a program manager, with no fixed weekly time.

locations.label: Mailing address, Friends Center building (mail only, no visitors)

cost.text: No volunteer fee is listed. Programs are funded by Impact Partners, and the pages list no participant fee.

first_step.how: Fill in the volunteer sign-up form on the Volunteer page. A program manager then contacts you to pick a grade range and schedule, and you attend a short training.
first_step.basis: The sign-up steps are spelled out in order, and a short training with a program manager comes before teaching. The page does not say whether teaching experience is needed.
first_step.what_to_expect: Expect a short training with a program manager, who answers your questions before you teach. You then choose a grade range from K to 12 and a schedule together, often at a class near your home or work. Classes can be in person or virtual.
first_visit_tips: Do not come to 1501 Cherry Street expecting an office: the address is for mail, and the office does not take visitors.
Call 267-519-5307 with questions before you fill in the form.
Think about the grade range you would like before the program manager calls you.

records.notes: The contact page lists a named staff email for information. It is left out so that one staff member's direct address is not published. The tier 1 contact name 'The Organization' is removed because it is not a person. The tier 1 season 'fall' is removed because the group runs school year programs. The events page lists about 20 volunteers per day for JA Finance Park and a 2026 to 2027 after school company program running November 3, 2026 to March 20, 2027 at sites across southeastern Pennsylvania; these dated items are not in schedule text.

notes: All seven groups in batch 057 are published at tier 2 with deep first-visit fields. Key findings: (1) Lynch Observatory public nights are paused while the telescope is replaced and no dates are set, so the newcomer rating is 2 and the record says so. (2) Junior Achievement's office is mail only and takes no visitors, so the record tells people to call. (3) JSJ Food Bank: a CBS article dated June 18, 2025 confirms a summer 2025 meal program for under 18s; no current sign-up route was found, and the one WebSearch was used for that gap. (4) Jewish Graduate Student Network has no dated evidence, so status stays probably_active with low confidence. (5) Japanese Christian Church has dated items through September 2026. (6) JCOR's email group page returned HTTP 402 and its Atom feed has no entries. Leads: the six JCOR shuls are listed with the directory page as the link. Not listed: Northeast Community Kollel (own website, not fetched this pass), the Folkshul partners page (not reviewed), and the JGSN student associations (no contacts, eligibility not stated). Budget: 1 of 1 WebSearch, 30 of 60 WebFetch calls, no more than 6 fetches per group.
